info.title: dian-einvoice
info.description:
The API of dian-einvoice, the same one its web app uses: contacts, items, invoices, credit and debit notes, their electronic document chain (UBL 2.1 XML, CUFE or CUDE, XAdES signature, transmission and the response), the delivery to the customer, and payments. In this project the DIAN is always a local simulator and every email lands in a local mailbox: nothing reaches the DIAN.

## Authentication

Send a company API key in the `Authorization` header: `Authorization: Bearer dei_...`. Owners and admins create keys in **Settings → Developers**. A key is shown once and only its hash is stored; it can expire or be revoked.

- The company is the key's company: `X-Company-Id` is not needed and, when sent, must be that company (403 otherwise).
- `read_only` keys read everything below. `read_write` keys also write contacts, items, invoices, notes and payments, and run their actions (issue, retry, resend, send again, void a payment).
- No key manages users, API keys, webhooks, certificates, DIAN settings or the simulator: those belong to the web app session, and keys get 403.
- In timelines, the actor of an action done with a key is the key, with its name.

## Idempotency

Any `POST` may carry an `Idempotency-Key` header (1 to 255 visible ASCII characters, such as a UUID). Keys are per company. Each one is kept 24 hours with the response and a fingerprint of the request (method, path and body).

- The same key with the same request returns the first response, status and body, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and runs nothing.
- The same key with another request returns **422**; while the first request is still running, **409**.
- Reserving a key is atomic, so two simultaneous requests with one key never both run. A 5xx response is not kept: the request can be repeated with the same key.

## Rate limits

Each key may make 120 requests per minute, unless it has a limit of its own. Every response to a key carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (Unix time), plus the IETF draft's `RateLimit-Policy` and `RateLimit`. Above the limit, the API returns **429** with `Retry-After` in seconds.

## Pagination and search

Lists return `data`, `links` and `meta` (`current_page`, `last_page`, `per_page`, `total`). Use `?page=` and `?per_page=` (1 to 100, 25 by default); most lists also take `?search=` and their own filters.

## Money and dates

Amounts, quantities and rates are decimal strings, such as `"1190000.00"`, never floats. Document dates are Colombian dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`); instants are ISO 8601 in UTC.

## Errors

Every error is `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457): `type` (always `about:blank`), `title`, `status`, `detail`, `instance`, `request_id` and `correlation_id`. Validation errors (422) add `errors`, each field's messages. Every response carries an `X-Request-Id` header and an `X-Correlation-Id` header with the same ids, which the logs also hold: quote them when asking about a request. 401: no valid credentials. 403: the key level or the role does not allow it. 404: not found in the company. 409: the state does not allow it, such as issuing twice. 503: a local service, such as the DIAN simulator, is not responding.

## Correlation

Every response carries `X-Correlation-Id`, the id of the journey the request begins: a lowercase ULID, such as `01jcz9w6n8s0k3q4r5t6v7w8x9`. What the request sets in motion carries the same id: the steps of the electronic document chain, the call to the DIAN, the email to the customer and every webhook delivery (in its own `X-Correlation-Id` header). To tie an integration's logs to the platform's, send your own id in `X-Correlation-Id`: it is kept when it is a ULID, in upper or lower case, and replaced by a new one otherwise. Problems return it as `correlation_id`.

## Webhooks

Owners and admins subscribe URLs in **Settings → Developers**: in production, an https URL on port 443, the default port of https, the only one deliveries leave on. Another scheme or port is refused when the subscription is created or changed, with a **422** whose `errors.url` says why, and before every attempt of a subscription saved before. They subscribe to these events: `invoice.issued`, `invoice.accepted`, `invoice.rejected`, `invoice.failed`, `invoice.delivered`, `invoice.paid`, `invoice.voided`; `credit_note.issued`, `credit_note.accepted`, `credit_note.rejected`, `credit_note.delivered`, and the same four for `debit_note`; `payment.recorded` and `payment.voided`. "Send test event" sends `webhook.test`.

The body is `{"id": "evt_...", "type": "invoice.accepted", "created_at": "...", "company_id": "...", "data": {"object": {...}}}`, where `data.object` is the same resource this API returns for that document or payment.

Deliveries follow the [Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com) specification: the headers `webhook-id` (the event id, the same on every retry), `webhook-timestamp` (Unix seconds) and `webhook-signature` (`v1,` and the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{body}` with the secret, the base64 after `whsec_` decoded), plus `X-Correlation-Id`, the journey of the request that caused the event. Verify the signature over the raw body, reject old timestamps, and respond with a 2xx within 5 seconds.

Delivery is at least once and in no particular order: deduplicate by `webhook-id`. A failed attempt is retried after 2, 5, 15, 45 and 120 seconds; then the delivery fails, and it can be sent again by hand. A subscription is switched off after 20 failed deliveries in a row.

get.description:
Drafts first, then issued documents from the newest number down.

Filters: ?status=draft|issued; ?electronic_status=pending|generated|signed|sending|accepted|rejected|failed,
or processing for the first four; ?from= and ?to= (the issue date, or the creation date of a
draft); ?search= (the number or the customer, and for a note its invoice's number); ?contact_id=
for one customer. Invoices also take ?balance_status=, ?payment_status=unpaid|partially_paid|paid
and ?overdue=1 (accepted invoices with something left to collect after their due date, or
after their issue date when paid in cash). Notes also take ?related_document_id= for the notes
of one invoice.

Rows are summaries: the frozen copies of the company, the customer and the numbering, and the
nested contact, come only with the detail.

credit.

get.description:
Drafts first, then issued documents from the newest number down.

Filters: ?status=draft|issued; ?electronic_status=pending|generated|signed|sending|accepted|rejected|failed,
or processing for the first four; ?from= and ?to= (the issue date, or the creation date of a
draft); ?search= (the number or the customer, and for a note its invoice's number); ?contact_id=
for one customer. Invoices also take ?balance_status=, ?payment_status=unpaid|partially_paid|paid
and ?overdue=1 (accepted invoices with something left to collect after their due date, or
after their issue date when paid in cash). Notes also take ?related_document_id= for the notes
of one invoice.

Rows are summaries: the frozen copies of the company, the customer and the numbering, and the
nested contact, come only with the detail.

and ?overdue=1 (accepted invoices with something left to collect after their due date, or
after their issue date when paid in cash). Notes also take ?related_document_id= for the notes
of one invoice.

Rows are summaries: the frozen copies of the company, the customer and the numbering, and the
nested contact, come only with the detail.

DeliveryStatus.description:
The delivery of an accepted document to its customer, apart from its electronic status. It starts when the local DIAN simulator accepts the document, and runs three queued steps (DeliveryStep) while pending: attached_document, pdf and email. Then it is delivered, or not_applicable when the customer has no email. A step that fails leads to failed; Send again, or Regenerate PDF when the PDF failed, takes it back to pending, and so does Send again after delivered or not_applicable. In this project the email always goes to the local development mailbox, so delivered means "the local mailbox accepted it", and nothing leaves the machine. Drafts and documents not accepted yet have no delivery status. | | |---| | `pending`
Building the AttachedDocument or the PDF, or packaging and sending the email. | | `delivered`
The mail server accepted the email with the zip. | | `failed`
A step failed, or every email attempt did; the reason is kept with the document. | | `not_applicable`
The customer has no email, such as the final consumer: the files exist, nothing is sent. |
DeliveryStatus.title: DeliveryStatus

DeliveryStep.description:
The three steps of the customer delivery, in order. Each one runs as one queued job. | | |---| | `attached_document`
Build the AttachedDocument (signed invoice and ApplicationResponse) and sign it. | | `pdf`
Draw the PDF, the graphic representation of the invoice, from its frozen copies. | | `email`
Package the AttachedDocument and the PDF in a zip and email it to the customer. |

responded, found, not_found, timeout, no_response, refused, server_error, invalid_response, client_error or abandoned; null while the call runs. | | |---| | `responded`

DocumentEventType.description:
Entries of a document timeline. Those of the transmission always refer to the local DIAN simulator, which is the only DIAN this project talks to. | | |---| | `created`
The draft was created. | | `issued`
Issued: numbered and final. Payload: number, full_number, cufe (the CUFE or CUDE) and, for a note, related_number. | | `xml_generated`
The UBL XML was generated; payload: run. | | `xml_signed`
The XML was signed; payload: run, certificate_serial, test_certificate, sha256 and size. | | `issue_date_moved`
FAD09e, CAD09e and DAD09e: the chain generated or signed the XML on a later day in Colombia, so the issue date and time moved to that moment, the due date by the same days, and the CUFE or CUDE was calculated again. Payload: run, step, previous_issue_date, previous_issue_time, previous_due_date, previous_key, issue_date, issue_time, due_date and key (the due date of a cash document is its issue date). | | `xml_failed`
Generation or signing failed; payload: step and reason. | | `transmission_attempt`
One call of an attempt: SendBillSync, or GetStatus when an earlier send may have arrived. Payload: run, attempt, operation, outcome, duration_ms, http_status, status_code, error, and retry_in and next_attempt_at when a retry was scheduled. | | `accepted`
Accepted by the local simulator; payload: status_code and notifications. | | `rejected`
Rejected by the local simulator's rules; payload: status_code and rules. | | `transmission_failed`
Every transmission attempt failed; payload: attempts and reason. | | `retry_requested`
Retry now, by a user; payload: step and whether it was waiting or failed. | | `resend_requested`
Resend after a rejection, by a user; payload: whether the CUFE changed. | | `attached_document_built`
The AttachedDocument was built and signed; payload: run, file_name, sha256 and size. | | `pdf_generated`
The PDF was generated; payload: run, file_name, pages, sha256 and size. | | `email_attempt`
One email attempt to the customer, always caught by the local mailbox. Payload: run, attempt, max_attempts, recipient, outcome (sent or failed), error, message_id, package, and retry_in and next_attempt_at when a retry was scheduled. | | `delivery_not_applicable`
The customer has no email address, so nothing was sent; payload: run and package. | | `delivery_failed`
A delivery step failed, or every email attempt did; payload: step, reason and attempts. | | `delivery_requested`
Send again, by a user; payload: run, recipient, previous_recipient and the step it starts from. | | `pdf_regeneration_requested`
Regenerate the PDF after it failed, by a user; payload: run and the step it starts from. | | `note_accepted`
On an invoice: the local simulator accepted one of its credit or debit notes. Payload: note_id, note_type, number, amount, voided and the balance_status it left. | | `payment_applied`
On an invoice: a payment was applied to it. Payload: payment_id, number, amount and balance. | | `payment_released`
On an invoice: a voided payment gave its amount back. Payload: payment_id, number, amount and balance. |

ElectronicStatus.description:
The state machine of an issued invoice's electronic document. Each step of the chain runs as a queued job that locks the document, checks that it is in the state the step expects, and moves it on: pending, generated, signed and sending, then accepted or rejected. Resend takes a rejected document back to pending. A failure in any step leads to failed, and Retry now starts again from the step that failed: pending, generated or signed. While sending, a transmission that failed for a transient reason waits for its next attempt; the document keeps the attempt number and the time of the next one. Drafts have no state. In this project the DIAN is always the local simulator, so accepted and rejected mean "by the local simulator", never by the DIAN. | | |---| | `pending`
Issued; the XML is about to be generated. | | `generated`
UBL XML built and stored, not signed yet. | | `signed`
Signed with the company certificate and stored; about to be sent. | | `sending`
Being sent, or waiting for the next attempt after a transient failure. | | `accepted`
Accepted by the local DIAN simulator, possibly with notifications. | | `rejected`
Rejected by the local DIAN simulator's rules; it can be sent again with Resend. | | `failed`
A step failed, or every transmission attempt did; Retry now starts again from that step. |
